# Incident Report — Network Forensic Analysis

**Source:** `2021-09-10-traffic-analysis-exercise.pcap` (9,221 frames, single capture file, no separate IDS export present in the evidence directory)

## 1. Infected Host

| Attribute | Value |
|---|---|
| IPv4 address | **10.9.10.102** |
| MAC address | **00:4f:49:b1:e8:c3** |
| Windows hostname | **DESKTOP-KKITB6Q** |
| Windows domain | angrypoutine.com (AD domain, DC at 10.9.10.9 / ANGRYPOUTINE-DC) |
| Logged-in user | **hobart.gunnarsson** (observed as Kerberos CNameString in AS-REQ/TGS-REQ traffic from 10.9.10.102 to the domain controller 10.9.10.9) |

Host identity is corroborated by DHCP (Option 12 hostname `DESKTOP-KKITB6Q`, requested IP 10.9.10.102, client MAC 00:4f:49:b1:e8:c3) and by NBNS name registrations for `DESKTOP-KKITB6Q<00>/<20>` and `ANGRYPOUTINE<00>` from the same IP.

## 2. Malware Family

**Behaviorally consistent with Qakbot (Qbot).** This is a **behavioral attribution, not signature-confirmed** — no Suricata/IDS alert export was present in the evidence directory, so no rule-name/SID match is available. The behavioral basis:

- Fake-old-browser delivery gate: a GET request using a spoofed `MSIE 7.0`/Windows NT 10.0 User-Agent string to a non-existent-elsewhere domain, at a randomized deep multi-segment URI path — a known Qakbot payload-gate pattern.
- The gate returned an `application/octet-stream` response with `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="date6"`, containing a 64-bit Windows PE **DLL** (not an EXE) — Qakbot's loader is典型ally delivered and executed as a DLL via `rundll32.exe`/regsvr32.
- Within 5 seconds of the DLL download completing, the host opened an HTTPS connection to a first C2 IP, followed by dozens of repeated short HTTPS connections to a second IP over the next ~74 minutes of the capture — classic Qakbot beacon-style C2 cadence.
- Both C2 IPs presented the **identical self-signed TLS certificate** (no SNI sent by the client), which is consistent with Qakbot's known practice of using self-generated certs for its encrypted C2 channel rather than a CA-issued cert or legitimate CDN.

## 3. Indicators of Compromise (all observed directly in the capture)

**Delivery / dropper:**
- Malicious domain: `simpsonsavingss.com` → resolved to **194.62.42.206**
- Malicious URL: `http://simpsonsavingss.com/bmdff/BhoHsCtZ/MLdmpfjaX/5uFG3Dz7yt/date1?BNLv65=pAAS`
  - Request time: 2021-09-11 03:17:27 (+0400)
  - User-Agent: `Mozilla/4.0 (compatible; MSIE 7.0; Windows NT 10.0; WOW64; Trident/7.0; .NET4.0C; .NET4.0E; .NET CLR 2.0.50727; .NET CLR 3.0.30729; .NET CLR 3.5.30729)`
  - Server response: `HTTP/1.1 200 OK`, `Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="date6"`, `Content-Type: application/octet-stream`, `Content-Length: 284816`
- Transferred file: server-labeled **`date6`** (delivered via URI `date1`), 284,816 bytes, PE32+ DLL (x86-64, GUI subsystem)
  - **SHA256: `eed363fc4af7a9070d69340592dcab7c78db4f90710357de29e3b624aa957cf8`**

**Command-and-control:**
- **167.172.37.9:443** — first C2 contact, opened 2021-09-11 03:17:31 (+0400), ~4.5 s after the dropper download finished; TLS handshake with no SNI extension
- **94.158.245.52:443** — persistent beacon C2, 35 separate TCP connections observed between 2021-09-11 03:17:36 and 04:31:24 (+0400), no SNI sent
- Shared self-signed TLS certificate on both C2 IPs, subject/issuer: `C=UK, ST=London, L=London, O=LL EST, OU=UK System, CN=londonareloeli.uk` (self-signed, subject == issuer)

**Not indicators (verified benign, ruled out during analysis):** all `*.microsoft.com`, `*.windowsupdate.com`, `*.msedge.net`, `*.office.com`/`officeapps.live.com`, `login.live.com`, `bing.com`, `msn.com`, `myexternalip.com`, and `footprintdns.com` traffic is standard Windows/Edge/Office telemetry and update traffic, unrelated to the infection.

## Summary Timeline (all times +0400, from capture)
| Time | Event |
|---|---|
| 03:15:09 | DESKTOP-KKITB6Q (10.9.10.102) DHCP lease / domain join traffic begins |
| 03:17:27 | GET to `simpsonsavingss.com` (194.62.42.206) — spoofed IE7 UA, delivers 284,816-byte x64 DLL |
| 03:17:31 | First HTTPS session to C2 167.172.37.9:443 |
| 03:17:36 – 04:31:24 | Recurring HTTPS beacon sessions (35 total) to C2 94.158.245.52:443, same self-signed cert |
